schema_version: v0 — skill-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The chaining skill over the chart device's question nexi: run the pre-build preamble as explicit, schema-gated stages. v0 carries ONE stage — orient (floor first, curtain held, the ceiling's mini agentic loop, the gate, the instance-space berth). Each later stage's prompt is TEMPLATE-FILLED from the previous stage's validated file as its nexus lands — a skipped stage is a build error, not a lapse.
why: Akien's skill-door facts (2026-07-28): CC skips steps when the answer looks visible; plain instructions get executed directly rather than routed through a skill; but /skillname fires reliably. So the preamble lives behind the slash-door — the one invocation path with physics rather than discipline behind it. The emitted packet is the inspectable artifact ('so we can inspect and improve what you're getting'); the schema gate at each handoff is the append-door pattern (Law 4). Device charter: cairn/machines/chart/intention+why.json; ticket: CairnCommons/tickets/chart-orient.json.
state: v0 — first cast 2026-07-28, one stage (orient). Grows a stage per landed nexus; /moreabout is the sibling learning door (its own stone).

nexus.note: SKILL.md carries the live sequence; this is the charter-face record.
nexus.routes_forward: orient packet berthed -> (later stages template-fill from it) -> the BUILD PACKET
nexus.routes_back: gate refusal -> fix the packet, never argue with the gate; ambiguity -> unknowns, never silent resolution

how_it_learns: Through the device's three mechanisms (deposit-back, /moreabout signals, the per-nexus dial) — the skill itself holds no state; it is the ceiling's vehicle. Its own learning surface: gate refusals during real use are gate-records for the nexus's exit schema (a field the ceiling repeatedly can't fill honestly is a schema defect, not a discipline defect).
traces_to: Law 1 (the preamble compiled; Claude spent on the novel)
Law 4 (schema-gated handoffs — step-skipping made a build error)
Law 3 (confidence and provenance as per-field data)
owner: the skills charter gates writes; Akien ratifies changes (signature gate). The packet berth is instance-space — never in git.

counted_by.what_it_counts: one berthed packet per door firing, the door's name as the filename prefix — so this is an EXACT count of chart-door firings, broken out per door. Measured 2026-08-04: 170 firings across eight doors between 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-03, which makes /chart the most-fired skill in Cairn.
counted_by.why_not_the_seam: chart already berths every firing through its own doors. Adding an input_contract would route each firing through cairn.machines.skill_block as well, berthing it twice at two addresses — and then 'how many times did /chart fire' would have two answers that could disagree. A skill is counted where it already leaves a mark; a second mark is not more measurement, it is a second thing to keep in sync (Law 1).
counted_by.the_descending_sequence_is_itself_a_datu: orient 25, survey 24, constrain 23, decompose 22, triage 21, hypothesize 20, validate 19, verdict 16. Twenty-five chains started and sixteen reached a verdict — 64%. Where a chain dies is readable straight off this count and nobody built anything to read it.

proof: the device's proof carries the machinery (cairn/machines/chart/proofs/test_chart_orient.py — 11 teeth, tester-sealed); the skill node additionally hangs the cairnmap recompile gate (IOU until cairnmap exists, per the skill class).
provenance: Cast 2026-07-28 inside the /sorted that fired stone 1 ('approved ratified make it so') — merged with the planned /chart-skill stone because the ceiling needs a runner (a nexus without its skill has no way to fire). Design: CairnCommons/notes/held-chart-nexus-extraction.json.
